extracted.intended_audience: aspiring creative writers and Coursera learners seeking to improve prose style
extracted.subtask_description: A Coursera module-based short course on prose style teaching clarity, word choice, imagery, economy, nouns & verbs, sensuous description, and revision through lectures, readings, and peer review assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style is choosable and developable
rubrics_metrics.description: Your style is as unique and distinctive as your face, your voice, except that you can choose it, you can work on it, enhance it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course framing: students are introduced to the idea that style can be consciously shaped; the course will teach techniques to develop and enhance an individual style through practice and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting pressure on written language
rubrics_metrics.description: We will introduce aspiring writers to the art of putting pressure on written language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied throughout modules: techniques and exercises aim to make words mean what you intend; emphasizes deliberate shaping of sentence-level choices to achieve intended meaning and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning, Sense, and Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on putting pressure on your words so that they mean what you intend. We balance abstraction with the need to make good sense. And we discuss the first and last stylistic difficulty of any prose writer, being clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module content includes 'Introduction to Meaning, Sense, and Clarity', 'The Pyramid of Language', 'Scatteration', examples of excellent word choice, and explicit instruction on clarity. Includes peer review and assignments to practice clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of metaphor and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: We will study the use of metaphor and imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taught as part of the craft of style to make prose vivid and expressive; paired with exercises and readings to show effective imagery in practice and how it supports meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice: clarity, grace, and inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how clarity, grace, and inventiveness in word choice are imperative to a story’s success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course offers videos ('Excellent Word Choice at Work'), readings, and close readings to show how precise, graceful, and inventive diction improves prose; practical exercises and peer feedback reinforce choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nouns and verbs as the building blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: We look at the various parts of speech and how two of them—nouns and verbs—are the building blocks of good style and good narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction emphasizes relying on nouns to make people, places, and things vivid and relying on verbs to keep the story alive and in motion; includes close readings and a 'Very Short Narrative' assignment to apply these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy (cutting unnecessary words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to take them out. And why: for humor, for clarity, for cleanliness, and for that fleet quality of wit that makes a style irresistible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module includes 'Surgery', a reading ('Informal List of Words and Phrases to Cut'), and a peer-reviewed assignment ('Cut It Out') focused on eliminating clutter and sharpening prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensuous description and concreteness ('No Ideas But in Things')
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the drive to get at ideas and feelings, with the need the story always has for concreteness, realness. We learn to express ideas in the form of physical things in a narrative world, to produce a style that speaks as much to the world of the senses as to the world of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module content ('An Introduction to Things', 'Concrete Style Infused with Thought and Feeling', close readings) and assignments teach how to ground abstract thought in sensory detail to make prose believable and affecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respecting the reader's mind and the reader–writer arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Respecting the Reader's Mind; The Reader-Writer Arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction on how to manage information, pacing, and revelation so prose honors the reader's expectations and comprehension; includes lectures and close readings illustrating strategies for guiding reader understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision skills and peer-review practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers will emerge with the revision skills essential to all writers of good stories and good prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course includes multiple peer-review assignments (each listed as ~120 minutes), 'Feedback Expectations for the Specialization', and assignment overviews designed to build revision techniques through critique and rewriting.
